George Pataki, New York’s last Republican governor — who defied scores of polls that year to win election — said Sunday there’s still time for GOP gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman to follow his lead to score the state’s top office.

Pataki said the only poll that counts is the one from the voters at the ballot box Tuesday.

The former gov defied his own odds, defeating three-term Democratic incumbent Gov. Mario Cuomo in 1994 — even though the final six polls preceding the election showed Cuomo ahead, including four by double digits.

“When I was running the first time [for governor in 1994] … the Sunday before the election … the [New York] Daily News straw poll came out, and it had never been wrong, and it showed me losing by 17 points [to Cuomo],” Pataki said on 77 WABC rado’s the “Cats Roundtable” program.

“I was down 17 with two days to go according to a poll that had never been wrong. And I ended up winning by 4. They were off by 21 points.

“If anybody knows to doubt the polls, it’s me because I’ve seen how inaccurate they can be,” Pataki told host John Catsimatidis.

The poll “that had never been wrong’’ had Cuomo up by 14 points.

Blakeman has ripped independent surveys conducted by Siena, Quinnipiac and Marist colleges claiming Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul has double-digit leads over him.

Still, demographically, the state is different from what it was in 1994. There are more enrolled Democrats today than there were three decades ago, fewer residents in more conservative upstate New York and more people living in deep blue New York City.

But Pataki has a point: Hochul defeated Republican challenger Lee Zeldin by just 6 points in 2022, despite Democrats having a huge 2-and-a-half-to-1 party enrollment advantage.

Pataki said there’s a big reason for common-sense voters of all stripes to vote for Blakeman, whom he praised for running an aggressive campaign touting tax cuts and slashing utility bills.

If Hochul wins, Pataki said, democratic socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani will be calling the shots in Albany.

“If we keep things the way we are, Mamdani — mark my words — is basically going to be telling the Albany politicians what to do. And that will mean higher taxes and other policies that hurt New York,” Pataki said.

“He’s already saying we need to raise taxes more, we need to spend more on programs that too often just waste all the money and put people into dependency,” he said.

But Pataki said he’s concerned that Republicans in New York unhappy with the status quo in Washington will sit out the election.

That would be a mistake, he said.

“This isn’t about Washington. This is about Albany, and we need change in Albany,” Pataki said.
news.content: پوشش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. جورج پاتاکی، آخرین فرماندار جمهوری‌خواه نیویورک - که در آن سال از نظرسنجی‌های زیادی سرپیچی کرد تا در انتخابات پیروز شود - یکشنبه گفت هنوز زمان برای بروس بلیکمن، نامزد فرمانداری حزب جمهوری‌خواه وجود دارد تا از پیشروی خود پیروی کند تا به دفتر عالی ایالت برسد. پاتاکی گفت: تنها نظرسنجی که سه‌شنبه رای‌دهندگان در یک رای به حساب می‌آیند. دولت سابق از شانس خود سرپیچی کرد و در سال 1994، فرماندار فعلی دموکرات ماریو کومو را شکست داد - حتی با وجود اینکه شش نظرسنجی نهایی قبل از انتخابات نشان می‌داد که کومو از جمله چهار عدد دو رقمی بود. پاتاکی در برنامه 77 رادوی WABC در برنامه «میزگرد گربه‌ها» با توجه به برنامه «میزگرد گربه‌ها» که 17 تا 2 روز بود، گفت: «زمانی که برای اولین بار [برای فرمانداری در سال 1994] کاندید شدم... نظرسنجی «دیلی نیوز» [نیویورک] منتشر شد، و هرگز اشتباه نبود، و نشان داد که من 17 امتیاز [نسبت به کومو] از دست دادم.» اشتباه شد و من با 4 برنده شدم. پاتاکی به مجری برنامه جان کاتسیماتیدیس گفت: «اگر کسی می‌داند به نظرسنجی‌ها شک کند، این من هستم، زیرا دیده‌ام که چقدر می‌توانند نادرست باشند.» نظرسنجی «هیچ وقت اشتباه نبوده است»، کومو را 14 امتیاز افزایش داده است. بلیکمن نظرسنجی‌های مستقل انجام‌شده توسط Siena، Quinnipiac و Marist کالج‌های Goocratich Hot Democratich را دو رقمی کرده است. با این حال، از نظر جمعیتی، ایالت با آنچه در سال 1994 بود متفاوت است. امروزه تعداد دموکرات‌های ثبت‌نام شده بیشتر از آنجاست

news.originalContent:
رسانه‌های ایران از درگذشت حمید علیدوستی، بازیکن سابق تیم ملی فوتبال ایران و باشگاه هما خبر داده‌اند.

به گزارش خبرگزاری ایسنا، آقای علیدوستی به دنبال «ابتلا به سرطان پروستات و استخوان در بیمارستان عرفان نیایش تهران به علت ایست قلبی» درگذشت.

آقای علیدوستی متولد ۲۱ اسفند ۱۳۳۴ بود و سابقه بازی در تیم ملی فوتبال ایران و باشگاه‌های هما، دارایی، کشاورز و سایپا را داشت.

او همچنین به عنوان سرمربی در تیم‌های پیکان، سایپا، هما، تراکتور، تیم زیر ۲۰ سال و زیر ۱۷ سال ایران فعالیت داشت.

از زندگی شخصی و ورزشی حمید علیدوستی فیلم مستندی به نام «سمفونی حمید» به کارگردانی و نویسندگی جعفر صادقی ساخته شده است که در سال ۱۴۰۰ در افتتاحیه جشنواره سینما حقیقت به نمایش درآمد و در آن جز چهره‌های سرشناس فوتبال ایران، ترانه علیدوستی دخترش هم حضور داشتند.

او از فوتبالیست‌هایی بود که هنر و موسیقی را جدی تعقیب می‌کرد و گفته نام دخترش را به دلیل عشقش به موسیقی ترانه گذاشته است.

او که در دهه شصت از معدود بازیکنانی بود که از باشگاهی جز استقلال و پرسپولیس به تیم ملی رسیده بود اولین لژیونر ایران در آلمان بعد از انقلاب محسوب می‌شود.

او سابقه مربیگری در باشگاه‌هایی مثل پیکان و سایپا و هما داشت و در تیم‌های هما، دارایی، کشاورز و سایپا بازی کرده بود.

او مدتی هم هدایت تیم‌های ملی فوتبال نوجوانان ایران را به عهده داشت.

آخرین فعالیت ورزشی آقای علیدوستی در تیرماه ۱۴۰۴ بود که به‌عنوان مدیر فنی و رئیس آکادمی باشگاه چادرملو اردکان معرفی شد. سال پیش از آن هم در تیم بهمن در لیگ دو مدیر فنی بود.

حمید علیدوستی یکی از شاخص‌ترین و فنی‌ترین مهاجمان فوتبال ایران محسوب می‌شد و در جام ملت‌های آسیا ۱۹۸۰ و ۱۹۸۴ مهاجم ثابت تیم ملی بود و در بازی‌های آسیایی ۱۹۸۲ و ۱۹۸۶ هم به میدان رفته و گل زده بود.

news.originalContent:
Alina Habba Mildon signed the lucrative contract while working at the Justice Department, before Trump pardoned the bank

US President Donald Trump has criticised one of his former lawyers for signing a contract worth more than $50 million with the family of a Venezuelan banker whom Trump later pardoned.

Alina Habba Mildon reportedly signed the lucrative deal while working as a federal prosecutor and later began working for the banker’s family while still being employed as an adviser to the US Department of Justice.

“I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous, and it’s not acceptable,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Florida on Saturday.

“Not acceptable at all,” he added.

According to The New York Times, Habba Mildon signed a four-year contract in October 2025 with a company owned by the family of Julio Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan banker who was seeking a presidential pardon.

Herrera was accused of bribing former Puerto Rico Governor Wanda Vazquez Garced in exchange for removing a financial regulator who was investigating his bank. He was facing federal bribery charges in the US before reaching a plea deal with prosecutors in August 2025.

Habba Mildon’s contract with his family’s company guaranteed her more than $50 million over four years, including an annual salary of $10 million and bonuses.

When she signed the deal, Habba Mildon was the acting US attorney for New Jersey, a position Trump had appointed her to after working as his personal lawyer.

She left that position in December after a court ruled she could not legally serve in the role. She then immediately took another job at the Justice Department as a senior adviser to the attorney general.

On January 1 , Habba Mildon officially began working for the banker’s family while still employed by the Justice Department.

Two weeks later, on January 15 , Trump granted Herrera a full presidential pardon.

The arrangement has raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, given Habba Mildon’s government position and her ties to Trump.

The company that hired her, Concord Partners, has no public profile and its business activities remain unclear, according to The New York Times.

Habba Mildon has denied having any role in securing Herrera’s pardon.

Last week, she said she had never been paid to obtain a pardon, had never discussed one with anyone at the White House or the Justice Department and had never worked to secure a pardon for anyone.

Trump was reportedly furious when he learned about the size of her contract.

The New York Times reported that he told aides and allies that Habba Mildon should donate some of the money to his future presidential library or another Trump-related organisation.

He also reportedly told at least one ally that Herrera’s family should stop paying her the remainder of the contract.

Speaking on Saturday, Trump said he told Habba Mildon he did not want her to be paid, describing the situation as “terrible”.

The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
news.content:
آلینا حبا میلدون زمانی که در وزارت دادگستری کار می کرد، قرارداد پر سود را امضا کرد، قبل از اینکه ترامپ بانک را عفو کند.
دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا از یکی از وکلای سابق خود به دلیل امضای قراردادی به ارزش بیش از 50 میلیون دلار با خانواده یک بانکدار ونزوئلایی که ترامپ بعداً او را عفو کرد، انتقاد کرد. طبق گزارش ها، آلینا حبا میلدون در حالی که به عنوان دادستان فدرال کار می کرد، این قرارداد سودآور را امضا کرد و بعداً در حالی که هنوز به عنوان مشاور وزارت دادگستری ایالات متحده مشغول به کار بود، برای خانواده بانکدار کار کرد. به گزارش نیویورک تایمز، هابا میلدون در اکتبر 2025 با شرکتی متعلق به خانواده خولیو هررا ولوتینی، یک بانکدار ونزوئلایی که به دنبال عفو رئیس جمهور بود، قراردادی چهار ساله امضا کرد. هررا متهم به رشوه دادن به فرماندار سابق پورتوریکو واندا وازکز گارسد در ازای اخراج یک سرمایه گذار مالی خود بود. او قبل از اینکه در آگوست 2025 با دادستان‌ها به توافق برسد، با اتهامات رشوه‌دهی فدرال در ایالات متحده مواجه بود. قرارداد حبا میلدون با شرکت خانواده‌اش بیش از 50 میلیون دلار را در طول چهار سال تضمین می‌کرد که شامل حقوق سالانه 10 میلیون دلار و پاداش بود. هنگامی که او قرارداد را امضا کرد، هابا میلدون به عنوان سرپرست جدید جرسی، ترامپ را به عنوان وکیل شخصی خود منصوب کرد.

FRANKFURT/BERLIN – Hooded rioters looted stores in Frankfurt late on Saturday after tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across Germany’s biggest cities to demand better education and lower living costs.

The protests followed a wave of Gen Z-led demonstrations across Europe this year. In Serbia, student-led activism helped unseat the country’s longtime leader at the ballot box, while protests in France have descended into rioting and looting.

The German protests organized by the campaign group “Gen Z regelt” — “Gen Z takes charge” in German — took place in 34 cities including Berlin, Frankfurt and Munich. The group says it opposes compulsory military service and wants greater investment in education as many young Germans struggle with rising costs.

In Frankfurt, Germany’s financial hub, at least two stores were looted as protests turned violent, with several more damaged and police trying to get the situation under control, according to a Reuters witness.

“Violent disturbances are continuing,” Frankfurt police said on X. “In the city center, windows have been smashed at several shops. Molotov cocktails are also being thrown at the emergency services. We urge all bystanders to avoid the city center or to leave the area.”

Official numbers on Saturday afternoon suggested turnout was below the 182,000 participants that organizers initially expected. Police in Frankfurt, Munich and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, half the roughly 36,000 on the organizers’ website.

German authorities said Saturday’s demonstrations, which coincide with Halloween festivities, had been largely peaceful, but warned of attempts by extremist groups to exploit the movement.

In Hamburg, some barricades had been set on fire.

“We are here today to fight for peace and freedom, rather than for war and coercion,” Gen Z regelt spokesperson Lina Friedrich said in Berlin on Saturday.

“What matters most to us is better support for the health and education systems. We are against compulsory military service and we are in favor of a fairer distribution of the burden.”

Parts of Germany’s far-left extremist scene and some groups linked to foreign extremist movements have joined efforts to mobilize support, according to the federal interior ministry.

“We all have those images from France in our minds — looting, burning houses, burning police vehicles, and attacks on police officers,” said Roman Poseck, interior minister for the state of Hesse, which includes Germany’s financial hub, Frankfurt.

“France must not be held up as a model in this regard.”

Some businesses across German cities boarded up windows and planned early closures ahead of the demonstrations due to concerns over possible unrest, including along Berlin’s luxury Kurfuerstendamm shopping boulevard.

Organizers have focused on what they see as the growing pressure on younger generations in Europe’s largest economy.

“The government has offered no response to our concerns other than to continue making cuts and piling further burdens upon us,” said Steve, an 18-year-old due to speak at a rally in Munich, addressing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

“We will continue to exercise our fundamental right to assemble until you stop ignoring us.”

Germany has struggled to revive economic growth. The country also faces growing pressure on pensions and public services as baby boomers retire and the working-age population shrinks.

Questions have been raised about who is driving the campaign and whether it is genuinely youth-led, given the broad mix of political and civil society groups involved.

Germany’s national school student umbrella organization, BSK, has distanced itself from the initiative and plans to hold a separate day of protest on Nov. 20.

Sean Baker, a student at the Technical University of Berlin, said he would join the protests on Saturday to call attention to the poor state of buildings on campus.

“When you go inside and enter the rooms, it looks like an abandoned building,” he told Reuters. “Yet this is where we’re expected to study on a regular basis.”

(Reporting by Miranda Murray, Timm Reichert, Tilman Blasshofer, Stephan Schepers and Martin Schlicht; Additional reporting by Christoph Steitz; Editing by Ros Russell, Joe Bavier, Alex Richardson and David Gregorio)

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. فرانکفورت/برلین - پس از آنکه ده‌ها هزار تظاهرکننده در سرتاسر بزرگترین شهرهای آلمان به خیابان‌ها آمدند تا خواستار آموزش بهتر و کاهش هزینه‌های زندگی شوند، شورش‌کنندگان کلاه‌دار فروشگاه‌های فرانکفورت را غارت کردند. در صربستان، فعالیت‌های دانشجویی به سرنگونی رهبر دیرینه این کشور در پای صندوق‌های رأی کمک کرد، در حالی که اعتراضات در فرانسه به شورش و غارت تبدیل شده است. اعتراضات آلمانی که توسط گروه کمپین «Gen Z regelt» - «Gen Z مسئولیت را به دست می‌گیرد» در آلمانی سازماندهی شده بود - در 34 شهر از جمله برلین، فرانکفورت و مونیخ برگزار شد. این گروه می‌گوید مخالف خدمت اجباری سربازی است و خواهان سرمایه‌گذاری بیشتر در آموزش است، زیرا بسیاری از جوانان آلمانی با افزایش هزینه‌ها دست و پنجه نرم می‌کنند. به گفته یکی از شاهدان رویترز، در فرانکفورت، مرکز مالی آلمان، حداقل دو فروشگاه به دلیل خشونت‌آمیز شدن تظاهرات غارت شد و چندین فروشگاه دیگر نیز آسیب دیدند و پلیس تلاش کرد اوضاع را تحت کنترل درآورد. در مرکز شهر، شیشه‌های چندین مغازه شکسته شده است. کوکتل‌های مولوتف نیز به سمت اورژانس پرتاب می‌شود.
ارقام رسمی بعد از ظهر شنبه حاکی از آن بود که شرکت کنندگان کمتر از 182000 شرکت کننده بود که سازمان دهندگان در ابتدا انتظار داشتند. پلیس در فرانکفورت، مونیخ و برلین تعداد آنها را گزارش داد

Katie Zacharia used Halloween to boast about her slim figure and designer duds online after setting the record for the shortest White House press secretary run in US history.

On the eve of Halloween, Zacharia posted a list of her attire on Oct. 13, the day of her one press briefing, detailing roughly $1,000 high heels, pricey blazer, and other attire totaling about $2,500.

She noted that her size was 00 “even after four kids” and crowed that she had no hair extensions or dye, that her blonde locks are all natural.

Fit Check for Halloween Fans:Veronica Beard Blazer and Skirt: Size 00, even after four kids.Christian Louboutin Miss Z in lamb nappa leather, 100 mm stiletto (sold out).Blouse: Nordstrom (sold out).Good luck! pic.twitter.com/YuV84UJxsT

“Good luck,” she added in an X post.

Later, she posted her dogs’ Halloween costumes, which spoofed Politico as “Paw-litico” and Washington Post as “Woofington Post.”

Zacharia lasted five days as White House press secretary from Oct. 12 through Oct. 16. Her abbreviated tenure broke the record 10-day record Anthony Scaramucci previously set as White House press secretary during the first Trump administration.

President Trump had selected her to succeed Karoline Leavitt, whom he frequently praised.

OG outfit + unusually friendly media! Happy Halloween! 🎃 pic.twitter.com/Om8EDO2QVO

In a split from many of her predecessors, Zacharia decided to hold a briefing on her second day in the job. Many White House press secretaries before her had taken more time to prep before their debut.

She gave a briefing for about 14 to 15 minutes, which was historically short. Her performance was widely panned, and many reporters said she seemed intimidated and not in command of the room.

Then she faced controversy over her claims to be a lawyer despite never passing the bar exam.

Zacharia was pressured out of her role amid the backlash and in the wake of tough interviews on Fox News. She is transitioning into a new role in the Trump administration that is not clear.

Last week, Zacharia jokingly expressed disappointment on Instagram that she wasn’t a more popular Halloween costume for trick-or-treaters this year.

“I hope you do dress up as me because it’s absolutely hilarious. We will be dressing up as a family. I will wear the OG costume and stay tuned to what my kids will be,” she told Newsweek.

Since departing the White House press secretary gig, Zacharia has indicated that she would be willing to serve in the role again in the future if asked by Trump.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. کتی زاخاریا پس از ثبت رکورد کوتاه‌ترین منشی مطبوعاتی کاخ سفید در تاریخ ایالات متحده، از هالووین استفاده کرد تا به صورت آنلاین به هیکل باریک و طراحان خود ببالد. در آستانه هالووین، زاخاریا لیستی از لباس‌های خود را در 13 اکتبر منتشر کرد، روزی که یک جلسه کوتاه مطبوعاتی کمتر از 0 دلار بود. کت بلیزر و سایر لباس ها به قیمت 2500 دلار. او خاطرنشان کرد که سایز او 00 است "حتی بعد از چهار بچه" و گفت که هیچ اکستنشن یا رنگ مو ندارد و موهای بلوندش همه طبیعی هستند. برای طرفداران هالووین مناسب بررسی کنید: ورونیکا ریش کتانی و دامن: سایز 00، حتی بعد از چهار بچه. Nordstrom (فروخته شد). موفق باشید! pic.twitter.com/YuV84UJxsT
او در یک پست X اضافه کرد: "موفق باشید." بعداً، او لباس‌های هالووین سگ‌هایش را منتشر کرد که پولیتیکو را با نام «Paw-litico» و واشنگتن پست را به‌عنوان «ووفینگتون پست» جعل کرد.
زاخاریا از 12 اکتبر تا 16 اکتبر پنج روز به عنوان سخنگوی کاخ سفید دوام آورد. دوره کوتاه او رکورد 10 روزه را که آنتونی اسکاراموچی قبلا به عنوان سخنگوی کاخ سفید در اولین دولت ترامپ ثبت کرده بود، شکست. پرزیدنت ترامپ او را به عنوان جانشین کارولین لیویت انتخاب کرده بود، که او اغلب از او تمجید می کرد. لباس OG + رسانه غیرمعمول دوستانه! هالووین مبارک! 🎃 pic.twitter.com/Om8EDO2QVO
در جدایی از بسیاری از اسلاف خود، زکریا تصمیم گرفت در دومین روز خود در این شهر یک جلسه توجیهی برگزار کند.

Belgrade’s chief prosecutor says arrest of Marko Kricak ‘has no link’ to elections that saw Aleksandar Vucic step down.

Serbian authorities have arrested the head of the country’s criminal police directorate on suspicion of abuse of office, while denying there are any links to elections held a week ago.

Marko Kricak, 42, was arrested on Sunday along with the police commander in charge of fighting organised crime, Bosko Sekulovic, Belgrade’s chief prosecutor said.

Prosecutor Nenad Stefanovic said the two were suspected of abusing their offices and failing to uphold their duties, “thus causing prejudice and serious harm to the rights of Belgrade’s former police chief”, Veselin Milic.

The allegations surfaced in an investigation into the murder of a suspected criminal underworld figure in a Belgrade restaurant in May.

Milic, who was arrested days after the murder for failing to report the crime and helping the perpetrator, began legal action while in custody against Kricak and Sekulovic, accusing them of giving prosecutors incomplete and false evidence.

Kricak is seen as a loyalist to defeated President Aleksandar Vucic. The police chief was accused by student groups of “brutality” in the police response to demonstrations that helped bring down Vucic’s ruling right-wing party.

Last week they demanded his removal, along with that of several other police and intelligence chiefs, as part of sweeping reforms.

However, the prosecutor’s office did not provide any link between Kricak’s arrest and the students’ demands.

“This arrest has no link with … the result of the legislative elections,” Stefanovic told journalists.

The Student List, a student-backed movement, won a historic victory on October 25 in snap elections called by Vucic after nearly two years of protests, ending 14 years of rule by his Serbian Progressive Party.

The arrests come as Serbia marks two years since the Novi Sad railway station disaster.

On Sunday, thousands gathered in Novi Sad to mark the day that a concrete canopy collapsed at the city’s newly renovated railway station, killing 16 people.

The crowd observed 16 minutes of silence, one for each victim, as the students marched silently through the rain carrying wreaths.

“It’s hard to go back to the place where it all happened,” Dijana Hrka, whose 27-year-old son Stefan was killed, told the AFP news agency. “I believe justice will be served.”

In a statement, students said “tragedy” was not enough to describe what happened.

“Tragedy describes an accident,” they said. “But behind that word, one can cleverly conceal the word we are all looking for: responsibility.”

The collapse set off Serbia’s biggest protests since the fall of former President Slobodan Milosevic in 2000. Prime Minister Milos Vucevic resigned in January 2025, and Vucic stepped down as president in September to lead his party’s list, pardoning students and activists prosecuted over the protests.
news.content: دادستان کل بلگراد می گوید دستگیری مارکو کریچاک «هیچ ارتباطی» با انتخاباتی که منجر به کناره گیری الکساندر ووچیچ شد، ندارد. مقامات صربستان رئیس اداره پلیس جنایی این کشور را به ظن سوء استفاده از مقام بازداشت کرده اند، در حالی که وجود هرگونه ارتباط با انتخابات یک هفته پیش را رد کرده اند. بوسکو سکولوویچ، دادستان کل بلگراد گفت، مارکو کریکاک، 42 ساله، روز یکشنبه به همراه فرمانده پلیس مسئول مبارزه با جرایم سازمان یافته دستگیر شد. دادستان نناد استفانوویچ گفت که این دو مظنون به سوء استفاده از دفاتر کار خود و کوتاهی در انجام وظایف خود هستند، "در نتیجه باعث تعصب و آسیب جدی پلیس به حقوق سابق بلگراد شده است." این اتهامات در تحقیقات مربوط به قتل یک شخصیت مظنون از دنیای اموات در بلگراد در یک رستوران بلگراد در ماه مه مطرح شد. میلیچ که چند روز پس از قتل به دلیل عدم گزارش جنایت و کمک به عامل جنایت دستگیر شد، در حالی که در بازداشت بود، علیه کریچاک و سکولوویچ، با متهم کردن آنها به ارائه ناقص و نادرست به دادستان ها و متهم ساختن مدارک نادرست به دادستان، اقدام قانونی را آغاز کرد.  رئیس پلیس توسط گروه‌های دانشجویی در واکنش پلیس به تظاهرات‌هایی که به سرنگونی حزب راست‌گرای حاکم ووچیچ کمک کرد، به «وحشیگری» متهم شد. هفته گذشته آنها خواستار برکناری وی به همراه چندین رئیس پلیس و اطلاعات دیگر به عنوان بخشی از اصلاحات گسترده شدند.

news.originalContent:

The Issue: Growing evidence that Rep. Ilhan Omar committed immigration fraud with a phony marriage.

If an immigrant breaks the law — whether by overstaying a visa or marrying one’s brother to get him a green card — all are offenses in the United States and should be prosecuted (“Feds ditched bro probe,” Oct. 30).

I don’t care if it’s Rep. Ilhan Omar or anyone else: They should be sent back to their country of origin if they commit immigration fraud or gain citizenship under false pretenses.

We have laws, rules and regulations in this country for a reason and it’s about time we enforce them.

Ilhan Omar is a five-star specimen for a hatchet job by President Trump: She’s a dark-skinned, Muslim female immigrant who’s a Democrat. Poor Omar has a lot going against her in Trump’s world.

It’s time to investigate the immigration history of all congressional office holders who are naturalized citizens. If federal investigators can harass the president for 10 years, then everyone should be subject to investigation. Nobody is above the law.

Don’t invite people into America who hate it. Omar is an antisemite who has contributed nothing to the welfare of the American people. Incredibly, Democrats will still defend her.

The Trump administration has presented me with an ethical dilemma: I’m thrilled that the Justice Department is investigating Omar, but I’m outraged that it’s investigating a candidate immediately before an election.

It looks like the America-hating, devout Muslim married her gay brother so he could live comfortably in the United States. Christmas has come early for me this year.

Should the Omar fiasco really surprise us? The investigations keep coming, from ex-Rep. Eric Swalwell to former FBI chief James Comey and more. If she’s guilty, stop dawdling, show her the door and move on to the rest of the backlog of dirty players.

The Issue: Gov. Hochul deflects questions about future tax increases ahead of Tuesday’s election.

Gov. Hochul never met a tax she didn’t like — until reelection rolls around (“Kat’s Damning Dodge,” Editorial, Oct. 30).

She did this in the 2024 elections with congestion pricing and is doing it again with the slew of tax hikes that Mayor Mamdani is proposing.

I hope New Yorkers are savvy enough not to be fooled again by this political huckster.

If reelected, Hochul will embrace Mamdani’s policies, raise taxes, go soft on crime and create another mass exodus from the state.

How can Hochul talk about affordability when she gives billions of taxpayer dollars to illegal immigrants?

She’s also trying to persuade voters with a one-time $200 utility rebate. My utilities have increased 30% in the last four years. What’s $200 going to do for me?

She also unleashed a $9 congestion toll — which amounts to $45 per week (or $2,340 per year) for commuters — after claiming she cares about the working class.

Not to mention she initially wanted the toll to be $15, then settled on $9 and claimed she was saving commuters $6 a trip.

New Yorkers — for their own good — need to dispose of this lying, failed governor.

news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر مشاهده کنید. مسئله: شواهد رو به رشد مبنی بر اینکه نماینده ایلهان عمر مرتکب کلاهبرداری مهاجرتی با ازدواج ساختگی شده است. اگر مهاجری قانون را نقض کند - چه با ماندن بیش از حد ویزا یا ازدواج با برادرش برای گرفتن گرین کارت - همه در ایالات متحده تخلف هستند و باید تحت پیگرد قانونی قرار گیرند. اگر Rep باشد ایلهان عمر یا هر کس دیگری: اگر مرتکب کلاهبرداری مهاجرتی یا اخذ تابعیت به بهانه های واهی شدند، باید به کشور مبدا بازگردانده شوند. ما به دلایلی قوانین، قوانین و مقرراتی در این کشور داریم و زمان آن فرا رسیده است که آنها را اجرا کنیم. ایلهان عمر یک نمونه پنج ستاره برای یک مهاجر مسلمان است. بیچاره عمر در دنیای ترامپ چیزهای زیادی علیه او دارد. زمان آن رسیده است که تاریخچه مهاجرت همه صاحبان مناصب کنگره را که شهروند تابعیت هستند بررسی کنیم. اگر بازرسان فدرال بتوانند رئیس جمهور را به مدت 10 سال مورد آزار و اذیت قرار دهند، پس همه باید تحت بازجویی قرار گیرند. هیچ کس فراتر از قانون نیست. افرادی را که از آن متنفرند به آمریکا دعوت نکنید. عمر یک یهودی ستیز است که هیچ کمکی به رفاه مردم آمریکا نکرده است. به طور باورنکردنی، دموکرات ها همچنان از او دفاع خواهند کرد. دولت ترامپ یک دوراهی اخلاقی برای من ایجاد کرده است: من از اینکه وزارت دادگستری در حال تحقیق درباره عمر است هیجان زده هستم، اما از اینکه این وزارتخانه در حال تحقیق از یک نامزد بلافاصله قبل از انتخابات است، خشمگین هستم.

The leaves are turning colors and starting to fall. You know what that means: College basketball is nearly here.

And the women’s season is filled with storylines.

JuJu Watkins, the presumed No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft, returns after a yearlong layoff, putting USC back into the spotlight.

Her return makes the conversation for National Player of the Year more interesting. Last season’s winner, Sarah Strong, headlines a UConn squad determined to get back to the mountaintop. Vanderbilt guard Mikayla Blakes, the breakout star of last season, Texas forward Madison Booker and Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo are among the candidates.

Dawn Staley’s South Carolina team is always a force to be reckoned with. But did the Big Ten finally overtake the SEC as the best basketball conference?

There’s so much to explore. But let’s start here, with The Post’s preseason Top 25:

After falling in last season’s national championship game to UCLA, expect the Gamecocks to return this season with vengeance on their mind. It doesn’t matter that they lost four seniors because Joyce Edwards, Chloe Kitts and Tessa Johnson are back. The Gamecocks also reloaded their roster with the additions of highly rated freshmen Jerzy Robinson and Oliviyah Edwards, and transfers Brooke Quarles Daniels (Michigan) and Jordan Lee (Texas).

Death, taxes and the Huskies having championship expectations. UConn went 38-1 last year but was bounced by South Carolina in the Final Four. Strong leads a talented roster featuring veteran guards KK Arnold, Ashlynn Shade and Kayleigh Heckel. The Huskies have an elite combination of scoring, defense and versatility, and they jam-packed their nonconference schedule full of heavyweights.

There’s no denying that the return of Watkins changes the Trojans’ ceiling entirely. Jazzy Davidson, the reigning Freshman of the Year, is expected to take a leap, and USC also welcomes the nation’s top recruiting class, headlined by Saniyah Hall.

After back-to-back Elite Eight appearances, Duke is eager to get over the hump and reach a Final Four for the first time since 2006. The Blue Devils have a lot of continuity, bringing back nine players from last season, including star Toby Fournier.

Expectations have never been higher for the Wolverines. Guards Syla Swords and Olivia Olson, now juniors, didn’t mince their words at Big Ten media days, saying their sights are set on winning a national championship. The Wolverines are coming off a 28-win season (tying a program high) and a third-place finish in the Big Ten with a program-high 15 conference wins.

Texas knocked off South Carolina to win the SEC tournament last season. The Longhorns then went to the Final Four for the second consecutive year but are trying to get to the national championship game that’s eluded the program for 40 years. Booker, a three-time All-American, leads a balanced Longhorns team with five freshmen.

The Cardinals are returning four of their five top scorers from last season, including guard Tajianna Roberts, who shot 35.3 percent from deep last season.

After finishing second in the Big Ten last season, Iowa has a roster that blends veteran talent (Ava Heiden, Chazadi Wright) with newcomers, including five-star high school recruit McKenna Woliczko and Georgia transfer Dani Carnegie.

Vanderbilt swept SEC coach (Shea Ralph), player (Mikayla Blakes) and freshman of the year (Aubrey Galvan) last season. All three are back as the Commodores look to continue their ascent into women’s basketball elite.

Flau’jae Johnson, now in the WNBA, was a key loss for the Tigers. They’ll rely on MiLaysia Fulwiley and Mikaylah Williams to lead the charge this season.

Despite being the defending national champions, the Bruins are practically playing with a new roster after their top six scorers from last season went to the WNBA.

Freshman guard Kate Harpring turned heads in the preseason averaging 23 points and seven rebounds. She’s the only freshman named to the Naismith Player of the Year watch list.

Sayvia Sellers, who led the Huskies with 18 points per game, and Avery Howell, who led the Big Ten in defensive rebounds, return as Washington looks to go on a deep run come March.

The Fighting Irish will go where Hidalgo — the 5-foot-7 dynamo who averaged 25.3 points and 5.6 steals last season — takes them.

Keep an eye on Clara Strack, who averaged 16.9 points and 10.1 rebounds last season and broke her own program record with 91 blocked shots.

There’s a lot of talent within the Ole Miss locker room, including Tennessee transfer Talaysia Cooper. But the lack of continuity might mean some early-season growing pains.

This looks like a rebuilding year for Mark Campbell’s program as the Horned Frogs underwent massive roster turnover, bringing back just one starter and three total players from last season.

The Buckeyes return four starters from last season’s NCAA Tournament team, including 2026 Dawn Staley Award winner Jaloni Cambridge, who averaged 23.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game.

Illinois’ roster continuity should bode well for making a third consecutive NCAA Tournament.

Bri McDaniel is set to make her highly anticipated return to Maryland’s rotation after missing nearly two years for an ACL recovery.

Aaliyah Chavez, one of the nation’s most exciting freshmen a season ago, is poised to be even better.

Coming off a 25-win season, Villanova was picked to finish second in the Big East behind UConn.

West Virginia has 10 newcomers and just two returners. The name you might recognize is Gia Cooke, who led the team in scoring at 15 points per game.

Tori McKinney suffered a season-ending knee injury in practice this month. It’s a bummer, but the Gophers still look to make noise in a loaded Big Ten.

Coach Molly Miller turned a 10-win program into a 24-win NCAA Tournament team in her first season. What does she have in store in Year 2?

Final Four: South Carolina, UConn, USC, Duke

It’s the first Sheridan Sunday of November 2026. So is this the month that Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser’s Yellowstone spin-off, Dutton Ranch, returns with new episodes?

We’ve got info on a new episode of Luke Grimes’ Yellowstone spin-off, Marshals, below. But what about Dutton Ranch‘s Season 2 premiere date?

Dutton Ranch Episode 9, “El Padrino,” saw Beth (Kelly Reilly) and Rip (Cole Hauser) battle Mariano’s (Raoul Max Trujillo) cartel men, who kidnapped Carter (Finn Little) before the end credits rolled. Meanwhile, Beulah (Annette Bening) and Oreana (Natalie Alyn Lind) were dealing with the unexpected death of Rob-Will (Jai Courtney), and Joaquin (Juan Pablo Raba) was recovering from possibly pulling the trigger.

So what does Dutton Ranch Season 2 have in store? When is Season 2 of Dutton Ranch coming out? Is Dutton Ranch on tonight, Sunday, November 1? What time is Marshals on tonight? And will there be a Dutton Ranch and Marshals crossover?

Here’s everything we know about Dutton Ranch Season 2 release date and more.

Sadly, no. But a new episode of Sheridan’s other Yellowstone spin-off, Marshals, airs on CBS tonight at around 8:30 p.m. ET. Start time may vary depending on when the earlier NFL game airing on CBS ends. But new episodes of Marshals will be available for next-day streaming on Paramount+.

On Wednesday, June 24, ahead of Dutton Ranch Episode 8, Paramount+ officially renewed the series for Season 2! And it’s no surprise! The series has a Certified Fresh 90% Tomatometer rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and according to a Paramount+ press release, “Dutton Ranch cemented itself as a smash-hit by amassing 12.9 million viewers globally in the 7 days following its premiere — marking the biggest Original Series launch in Paramount+ history. The series also delivered 2.9 million total viewers during its two-episode debut on Paramount Network on May 15, making it the biggest series premiere on cable since 2023. With 1.85 million viewers for the premiere telecast alone, Dutton Ranch also ranked as the #1 cable entertainment telecast among both adults 18-49 and total viewers.”

“Dutton Ranch has resonated with audiences in a powerful way, building on the legacy of beloved characters, while establishing its own identity,” said Matt Thunell, President of Paramount Television Studios. “Thank you to our partners at Paramount+ and 101 Studios for a phenomenal first season. We look forward to bringing fans more stories from these unforgettable characters in Season 2.”

While there’s no official Dutton Ranch Season 2 premiere date on the books yet, The Hollywood Reporter confirmed that production is expected to begin early next year. “We’re slated to start early 2027 to film,” Reilly told THR in July. “But the room starts up pretty quick. I think we’re going to be very much involved in the room, so the next sort of six months is all about writing it.”

Assuming production sticks to the predicted timeline, here’s hoping Dutton Ranch Season 2 will premiere in 2027 rather than 2028. Stay tuned for more updates!

After recent feud escalation rumors between Hauser and Sheridan, some fans are fearful that Cole Hauser could be leaving Dutton Ranch ahead of Season 2. While the creator and star certainly share history, as far as we know, Rip isn’t leaving Dutton Ranch, nor is Cole Hauser! The Yellowstone spin-off was specifically written to continue Beth, Rip, and Carter’s stories — plus, Hauser is an EP on the series. So we don’t expect to say goodbye to Beth’s partner in crime any time soon.

When Dutton Ranch returns, however, it will have a new showrunner in Benjamin Cavell, who joined the team ahead of Season 2. Season 1 showrunner Chad Feehan departed from the series just three weeks before its premiere.

While Dutton Ranch doesn’t have a Season 2 premiere date yet, Sheridan’s other Yellowstone spin-off Marshals is already back!

Marshals Season 2, Episode 5 premieres Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 8:30 p.m. ET on CBS, with streaming on Paramount+. Here’s how to watch.

Grimes confirmed that Beth and Rip won’t be on Marshals Season 2 this fall. But with Dutton Ranch expected to film Season 2 in 2027, there’s still hope that Kayce could appear on Marshals‘ sister series — especially recent comments about a Dutton sibling reunion from Grimes and Marshals star Ash Santos.

“It’s not out of the question that we might have some sort of crossover at some point. Beth’s basically Kayce’s only living family member other than Tate. It would make sense that down the line we’d at least talk,” Grimes told TV Insider. “[Kelly and I] texted about it back and forth a lot, talked about how it’d be fun and necessary for our story arcs, however they’re going to end.”

When DECIDER asked Santos if she’s on board for a crossover, she said, “Hopefully. It would be cool. I agree with the fans. It’s hard not to want that, especially because Kayce was so close with Beth, and they had such an interesting brother-sister dynamic. I’m like, ‘Who wouldn’t want to see that?’”

The promising comments came just months after Reilly and Hauser shared their own positive sentiments, so if you’re in line for a Marshals and Dutton Ranch crossover episode, stay in line!

While we wait for Season 2 news, if you’re looking to watch or rewatch Dutton Ranch Season 1, it’s available to stream on Paramount+. Read on for more info, including where you can watch Dutton Ranch for free…

Paramount+ offers two subscription plans, Essential and Premium. Right now, you can get started with a seven-day free trial on the Premium plan.

The ad-supported Essential plan typically costs $8.99/month, while the ad-free Premium plan (which comes with Showtime titles and live CBS) costs $13.99/month.

Though Paramount+ doesn’t directly offer a free trial, you can get a seven-day free trial by adding Paramount+ Premium to your Prime Video account on Amazon ($13.99/month after the free trial).

If you have a cable login, you can also watch Dutton Ranch on Paramount Network. No cable login? No problem! Paramount Network is also included with an active subscription to Philo, Fubo, Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV, DIRECTV, or Sling TV. (Philo Essential ($25/month) offers a seven-day free trial, and Fubo, Hulu, DIRECTV, and YouTube TV also provide free trials for eligible subscribers.)

news.originalContent:
The UK PM’s statement comes as Commonwealth nations meet in Antigua and Barbuda.

The United Kingdom’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said his country is open to apologising for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade but ruled out reparations, which campaigners have for years called for.

Burnham wrote in an opinion article in The Guardian on Friday that Britain would also work on debt restructuring for the poorest countries, marking an historic turn in London’s stance.

The move comes ahead of a four-day summit starting Sunday of the 50-plus Commonwealth nations formerly colonised by Britain. The UK’s King Charles, who arrived in the Caribbean last week, is hosting the leaders in St John’s, the capital of Antigua and Barbuda.

“I want to express my sorrow and regret for the pain and suffering of so many millions of people, and to recognise the way it still shapes our world today,” Burnham wrote, in what amounted to a personal apology.

Caribbean nations that have more forcefully demanded reparations in recent years said they expect more from Britain, while opposition Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has criticised Burnham’s move as “navel-gazing”.

Transatlantic slavery lasted between the 16th and 19th centuries and saw some 12 million enslaved Africans torn from their homes and forcibly transported on ships to the Americas with the help of local warlords. Enslaved people were sold on plantations and as domestic workers, and their labour produced goods that built wealth in Europe.

Britain and Portugal accounted for about 70 percent of all Africans exported to the Americas, while France, Spain and the Netherlands also traded in significant numbers of enslaved people. Britain alone transported 3.1 million Africans to British colonies in the Caribbean, the Americas and other countries, according to its national archives. Only 2.7 million arrived, as many perished in treacherous sea journeys.

British abolitionists began campaigning against slavery in 1787, particularly in cities like Manchester. In 1807, Parliament passed the Slave Trade Act, essentially banning new enslavement. More than three decades later, in 1834, Britain banned slavery in its entirety, although the practice continued for several years.

Amid calls for accountability in 2006, then-Prime Minister Tony Blair expressed “deep sorrow” for Britain’s role in the slave trade, but fell short of apologising or speaking about reparations.

Burnham’s apology came during Britain’s Black History Month and as the Commonwealth is meeting in Antigua and Barbuda.

In his article, the British prime minister said London wants to keep diplomatic and trade ties with its Commonwealth allies.

“In an increasingly divided and dangerous world, our family of nations in the Commonwealth is vital to our interests,” he wrote, adding that Britain “can seize opportunities for trade and economic collaboration”.

Britain will allow the most vulnerable countries to repay their debts over a longer period, he added, with former Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, who spearheaded the UK’s 1991 initiative to reduce debt for poorer countries, leading the charge.

Since 2013, the Caribbean Community and Common Market (CARICOM) has called on Western countries involved to acknowledge their role and institute monetary reparations for slavery.

In recent years, those calls have grown louder, led by Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley.

Ghana, where around 10-15 percent of enslaved people were transferred from, has also played a major role and pushed a historic resolution at the United Nations in March that saw 123 countries vote to declare trafficking of enslaved Africans the gravest crime against humanity. All European nations abstained while the United States, Israel and Argentina voted against the measure.

Campaigners argue that there is a legal and moral case for financial payment and debt cancellations for the centuries of damage caused by enslavement. Those damages, they say, are evident in the structural inequalities that continue to plague countries where human capital was stolen from and those in the Caribbean that faced genocides after Europeans arrived.

They also point to the loss of lives, the erasure of cultures, the looting of artefacts in the colonial era that followed, and ongoing economic disparities and development challenges that see those nations struggle to access international financial institutions.

In June, Mottley announced a 19-point manifesto at a conference in Ghana, as Caribbean and African countries increasingly align to more strongly push their case. It called for a “full and formal apology”, monetary compensation from nations, but also institutions, including corporations and churches. It also called for technology transfer, education and healthcare funding, debt relief and economic development. The plan revised an earlier CARICOM 10-point plan.

“We live in a world today where people call out people for everything, for misogyny, for sexual assault, for all kinds of behaviour. But yet we have not found the moral courage to state unanimously across humanity that this grave crime against humanity that persisted for centuries ought to be declared so by all,” Mottley said at the conference.

European nations, including Britain, argue that those crimes were committed long ago and that, as such, their people should not pay for them. Some also point to the role of local African chiefs who worked with the Europeans to kidnap and enslave people.

“I do not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played no personal part,” Burnham wrote in The Guardian.

Instead, he said, the UK was “offering a structured dialogue” with those affected and debt restructuring.

France recognised slavery as a crime against humanity in 2001. In May, French President Emmanuel Macron said Paris should look into reparations, but did not make clear proposals.

In 2022, the Netherlands apologised for its role.

The Church of England, whose clergy also owned enslaved people, set up a fund of 100 million British pounds ($134mn) to cater to affected communities and to conduct further research into slavery’s legacies.

In a statement, Saint Lucia’s Prime Minister Philip J Pierre, who currently chairs CARICOM, said the organisation rejects the argument that Britain of today cannot be held responsible for slavery.

“Reparatory justice has never been about individual guilt. It is about the responsibility of states and institutions — and that responsibility does not expire with the passing of generations,” he said. Without repair, PM Burnham’s apology was “incomplete”, he added.

Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama said he welcomed Burnham’s statement with “caution” and reiterated the need for a formal apology, targeted investments in several sectors, and an international commitment to “dismantle systemic racism and Afrophobia”.

Denis O’Brien, founder of the advocacy group The Repair Campaign, also said London “must stop obfuscating and give a full and formal apology now”.

The UK’s opposition Conservative Party leader Badenoch kicked against the move entirely in a post on X, and asked whether the descendants of African rulers involved would also be asked for reparations.

“There is no reason British taxpayers today should be held financially responsible for things that happened generations before any of us were born,” she said.

“Labour are already spending too much on Britain’s welfare state, now is not the time for Andy Burnham to be providing global welfare.”

Meanwhile, Bell Ribeiro-Addy, chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for Afrikan Reparations, which endorses compensation, welcomed Burnham’s steps but said action was still “lacking”.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

If Sarah J. Maas’s “fairy smut” has you needing backup for your ‘wettest moments’, this underwear brand is here to absorb the blow — up to 11 super tampons’ worth, to be exact.

Underwear brand Knix has launched a spicy new collection in collaboration with Sarah J. Maas, author of the hit fantasy-romance series “A Court of Thorns and Roses.”

Knix CMO Cynthia Leo isn’t shying away from the raunchy theme. “We make leak-proof underwear, and the books are a little saucy,” she quipped, “so we wanted to be there for all of your wettest moments.”

The cheeky ACOTAR x Knix line claims its leak-proof underwear absorbs the equivalent of “up to 11 super tampons.” The brand markets itself on being eqipped to handle period blood, sweat, pee and discharge.

Maas’ book series debuted in 2015, and the viral franchise has since inspired merchandise collabs ranging from Sam’s Club throw blankets to $700 ball gowns.

The new line features sets themed around the series’ fictional courts: floral pairs for the Spring Court and seductive lingerie made for “deep bonds and a little spice” for the Night Court.

The Autumn and Summer Courts get their own inspired designs, alongside merch featuring popular series catchphrases like a t-shirt that says“ darling” and another with the “bat boyfriends” – based on the male characters.

Knix teamed up with 40 diehard fans to help design the collection. Influencers flown to New York for the brand launch praised how the line channeled Maas’ strong female characters.

A major goal of the crossover is to appeal to long-time readers and series newcomers alike, trying to keep the designs universal. It joins a growing list of ACOTAR lingerie partnerships—including For Love and Lemons’ fairy-core fashion line, featuring underwear labeled with the male characters’ names.

Fairy smut is a sub-genre of “Romantasy” (romance and fantasy) where the fairy men are muscular, mythical men who have magic and powers. The fairy men typically fall in love with a human girl, have lots of sexual encounters and then the girl becomes a fairy too.

Their wings and powers make the characters have abstract sex – where they can sometimes read each other’s minds, have sex mid-air, or cause destruction.

Maas has frequently defended the explicit romantic themes in her books, pushing back against critics who dismiss the genre. She has spoke out on podcasts to call out critics who use the phrase ‘smut’ to dismiss her work and the misogyny behind those who think smut is unserious literary work.

“I find that there is a tendency for people to roll their eyes at things that bring joy. And bring women joy, especially. And it pisses me the fuck off constantly,” Maas shared on the Call Her Daddy podcast with Alex Cooper.

Fans of the series have mixed feelings about the new line, with some fans commenting that the line ‘isn’t whimsical enough’ and looks ‘too basic.’

“We need whimsical, magical, royal. These garments could have been in the collection of any department store. I don’t see ACOTAR in any of this,” quipped one user.

But others think the leakproof underwear will be a big help when reading the newest book.

“Gorgeous AND can stand the test of watery bowels?? Sign me up,” said one Instagrammer.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر مشاهده کنید. اگر "پری smut" سارا جی ماس نیاز به پشتیبان برای "مرطوب ترین لحظات" خود دارد، این برند لباس زیر اینجاست تا ضربه را جذب کند — به طور دقیق، تامپون تا 11 فوق العاده ارزش دارد. برند لباس زیر Knix مجموعه جدید تند و تند و تند سری Faisy را با همکاری Sarah-romaاس راه اندازی کرده است. "صحنه ای از خار و گل رز." سینتیا لئو مدیر ارشد اجرایی Knix از موضوع پرخاشگر دوری نمی‌کند. او با کنایه گفت: «ما لباس‌های زیر ضد نشتی درست می‌کنیم، و کتاب‌ها کمی تند و تیز هستند، بنابراین می‌خواستیم برای تمام لحظات مرطوب شما آنجا باشیم.»
لاین ACOTAR x Knix بی‌پرده ادعا می‌کند که لباس‌های زیر ضد نشتی آن معادل «۱۱ تامپون فوق‌العاده» را جذب می‌کنند. این برند برای کنترل خون، عرق، ادرار و ترشحات پریود خود را به بازار عرضه می کند. مجموعه کتاب‌های ماس در سال ۲۰۱۵ عرضه شد و از آن زمان این مجموعه‌ی ویروسی الهام‌بخش همکاری‌های تجاری از Sam’s Club گرفته تا لباس‌های مجلسی ۷۰۰ دلاری است. خط جدید ویژگی‌های مجموعه‌ای با مضمون زمین‌های داستانی مجموعه دارد: جفت‌های گلدار برای دادگاه اسپرینگ و لباس‌های زیر زنانه اغواکننده ساخته شده برای لباس زیر زنانه کوچک برای لباس‌های کوچک. دادگاه‌های پاییز و تابستان طرح‌های الهام‌گرفته خود را دارند، در کنار کالاهایی که شامل عبارات جذاب سریال‌های محبوب مانند تی‌شرتی است که روی آن نوشته شده است «عزیزم» و دیگری با «دوست پسر خفاش» - بر اساس شخصیت‌های مرد. Knix با 40 طرفدار سرسخت همکاری کرد تا به طراحی مجموعه کمک کند. اینفلوئنسرها برای معرفی برند به نیویورک پرواز کردند

news.originalContent:
Protesters march in New Delhi demanding the election chief quit over voter roll changes seen as favouring Modi’s party.

Thousands have marched through New Delhi demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner over changes to voter lists that opposition parties say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

Rahul Gandhi of the Indian National Congress led Sunday’s protest, the latest in more than a month of demonstrations accusing Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of overseeing a biased revision of electoral rolls.

Opposition leaders say the removal of more than 130 million names disproportionately affected Muslims and other minorities, who are less likely to back Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and says voters whose names were wrongly deleted can re-register.

The BJP has accused the opposition of undermining democracy by challenging legitimate procedures.

India’s next general election is scheduled for 2029.
news.content: تظاهرات کنندگان در دهلی نو خواستار استعفای رئیس انتخابات به دلیل تغییرات فهرست رأی دهندگان به نفع حزب مودی شدند. هزاران نفر در دهلی نو راهپیمایی کردند و خواستار استعفای رئیس کمیسیون انتخابات هند به دلیل تغییرات در فهرست رأی دهندگان شدند که احزاب مخالف می گویند به نفع حزب حاکم نارندرا مودی، نخست وزیر است. راهول گاندی، از کنگره ملی هند، اعتراض روز یکشنبه را رهبری کرد، آخرین تظاهرات در بیش از یک ماه تظاهراتی که گیانش کومار، رئیس کمیسیون انتخابات را متهم به نظارت بر بازنگری مغرضانه فهرست‌های انتخاباتی کرد. رهبران اپوزیسیون می‌گویند که حذف بیش از 130 میلیون نام به احتمال زیاد مسلمانان و سایر اقلیت‌های هندی هندی را که کمتر از هندوها هستند، متاثر می‌شود. حزب (BJP). کمیسیون انتخابات حمایت از هر حزبی را رد کرده است و می گوید رای دهندگانی که نام آنها به اشتباه حذف شده است می توانند دوباره ثبت نام کنند. BJP مخالفان را به تضعیف دموکراسی با به چالش کشیدن رویه های قانونی متهم کرده است. انتخابات عمومی بعدی هند برای سال 2029 برنامه ریزی شده است.

news.originalContent:
The mandate for UN mission that was tasked to monitor 1991 truce and hold referendum in disputed territory expires.

Morocco has welcomed the defeat of a US-drafted resolution which sought to extend the mandate of the UN mission in the disputed Western Sahara.

The mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) expired on Saturday after a veto by Russia, leaving the future of the peacekeeping mission in limbo. In 1991, the UN established MINURSO to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum on the territory’s future.

Morocco has considered Western Sahara its own territory since 1975, when Spain withdrew from the desert region in northwest Africa which is roughly the size of Britain. The Algeria-backed Polisario Front seeks to establish an independent state called the Sahrawi Republic.

So, why is Morocco celebrating the failed UN resolution? What does it mean for the future of the disputed region?

On Friday, the US, which is a permanent member of the UN Security Council, proposed a resolution to support the principle of self-determination in the disputed Western Sahara.

Russia vetoed the resolution, despite support from 11 of the 15 council members, including fellow permanent members France and the United Kingdom.

The US draft would have extended the mission for a year, removed “referendum” from its name and made Morocco’s autonomy proposal the only basis for further talks.

Last October, the UN Security Council adopted a resolution that offered genuine autonomy to Western Sahara. Under that plan, the territory would manage its internal affairs, but remain under Moroccan sovereignty.

The Security Council had already made the proposal a basis for negotiations last year and asked UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to submit a review of the peacekeeping mission.

Speaking after the vote, US ambassador Mike Waltz said it was truly unfortunate that in 2026 the veto was used to “preserve the letter R (in the Mission’s name) for referendum”.

He added that Washington’s proposal “would have moved the 50-year conflict forward” and added that the status quo is not acceptable.

Russia’s UN ambassador, Vassily Nebenzia, said at the same meeting that Moscow opposed the draft because it favoured one side.

“We stress the fact that the Security Council cannot automatically predetermine matters relating to sovereignty,” he said.

Instead, Russia proposed renewing the existing mission without those changes. But that draft also failed to secure the nine votes needed for adoption, receiving two votes in favour, one against and 11 abstentions.

MINURSO’s mission has 155 military personnel and is set to cost $62m in the fiscal year that began in June, according to a UN report. But its mandate expired on Saturday.

Morocco’s royal palace welcomed the failure to renew MINURSO, saying on Friday that UN personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days and that the Western Sahara issue should now be withdrawn from the Security Council’s consideration. Morocco said it remained committed to the ceasefire.

According to a UN media statement, Morocco’s UN representative also questioned why Algeria’s delegate was giving the Security Council “lectures” on the Western Sahara.

“Let these people [in the Western Sahara] go back to Morocco,” he said, “let them go home”.

Algeria expressed regret on Saturday over the failure to renew MINURSO’s mandate. Its foreign ministry criticised what it described as the US draft’s excessive bias towards Morocco.

According to a UN media statement, Algeria’s delegate to the UN thanked Russia for its draft resolution and all other member nations “who have chosen not to associate themselves” with an egregious injustice and a flagrant attack on “the very foundation of our organisation”.

Algeria’s UN representative noted that the country has been a refuge for hundreds of thousands of Sahrawi people who have been denied their right to self-determination.

The “tragedy being endured by the Sahrawi people has oddly been diluted to the concept of refugee populations”, he added.

Sidi Omar, the Polisario Front’s representative at the UN, told reporters on Friday that he welcomed Russia’s veto because the US proposal would undermine Sahrawi self-determination.

The Polisario Front, the political and military representative, does not recognise Morocco’s annexation of the territory following Spain’s withdrawal in 1975. It has been seeking a UN-supervised referendum for self-determination.

In 1976, it declared the independent Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic.

Decades of fighting drove at least 170,000 Indigenous people into refugee camps in Tindouf in neighbouring Algeria, which backs the Polisario Front.

The Polisario Front signed a UN-brokered ceasefire with Morocco in 1991. It called for a referendum within six months, but it was never held.

Morocco, which retains control of its lucrative phosphate and fishing resources in Western Sahara, claims historic and pre-colonial ties to the land and views the region as an integral part of its territory [“Greater Morocco”].

For decades, the US has provided military and diplomatic support to Morocco. But in 2020, Donald Trump recognised Moroccan sovereignty over the territory during his first term in office. Morocco soon established diplomatic ties with Israel as part of the so-called Abraham Accords.

The region is now the last United Nations-designated “non-self-governing territory” in Africa, where between 100,000 and 140,000 Moroccan military personnel are based.

Low-level fighting has also continued since the Polisario Front said it was resuming armed struggle in 2020.

MINURSO was set up to monitor the 1991 ceasefire and hold a referendum in Western Sahara. The expiry of its mandate will likely boost Morocco’s stance on the referendum question, though its autonomy proposal has already been adopted by the UN.

On Saturday, according to a video report by the Reuters news agency, a festive atmosphere prevailed in the streets of El Aaiun, the capital of Western Sahara.

In the central Mechoua Square, dozens of people were wearing melfas, the traditional Sahrawi women’s garments, and long robes known as darra, as they waved Moroccan flags and displayed portraits of Morocco’s King Mohammed VI.

Selim Balouati Lakhloufi, a historian and researcher based in Morocco, said that Morocco is pleased because “diplomatic developments at the United Nations are supporting its strategy regarding the [disputed Western] Sahara”.

“The support of powers such as the United States, France and the United Kingdom for Morocco’s autonomy proposal strengthens its international position and is gradually shifting the debate away from the right to self-determination and the possibility of independence toward a solution based on autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty,” he told Al Jazeera.

The collapse of MINURSO’s mandate could escalate the dispute in the Western Sahara, according to aid organisations.

Oxfam has warned that losing MINURSO’s “monitoring and de-escalation functions risks undermining security and stability”.

Lakhloufi said that the UN mission’s expiry is also unfavourable for Sahrawi independence aspirations.

Regarding the future of the Western Sahara, he said that Morocco will likely continue to consolidate its territorial, economic and administrative control, while the Polisario Front will face greater difficulties in securing international support.

“The proposal for autonomy could end up becoming the main framework for negotiations, pushing independence further and further out of reach,” he added.
news.content: مأموریت مأموریت سازمان ملل متحد که موظف به نظارت بر آتش بس سال 1991 و برگزاری همه پرسی در سرزمین های مورد مناقشه بود، منقضی می شود. مراکش از شکست پیش نویس قطعنامه ای توسط ایالات متحده که به دنبال تمدید مأموریت مأموریت سازمان ملل در صحرای غربی مورد مناقشه بود، استقبال کرده است. مأموریت هیئت سازمان ملل متحد برای همه پرسی در صحرای غربی پس از خروج از روسیه در آینده (MINURSO) پس از رفراندوم آینده در صحرای غربی به تصویب رسید. ماموریت حفظ صلح در بلاتکلیفی در سال 1991، سازمان ملل متحد MINURSO را برای نظارت بر آتش‌بس و آماده‌سازی یک همه‌پرسی در مورد آینده این قلمرو تأسیس کرد. مراکش از سال 1975، زمانی که اسپانیا از منطقه بیابانی در شمال غرب آفریقا که تقریباً به اندازه بریتانیا است، صحرای غربی را قلمرو خود در نظر گرفت. جبهه پولیساریو مورد حمایت الجزایر به دنبال ایجاد یک کشور مستقل به نام جمهوری صحرای است. پس چرا مراکش قطعنامه شکست خورده سازمان ملل را جشن می گیرد؟ چه معنایی برای آینده منطقه مورد مناقشه دارد؟ روز جمعه، ایالات متحده که یکی از اعضای دائم شورای امنیت سازمان ملل است، قطعنامه ای را برای حمایت از اصل خودمختاری در صحرای غربی مورد مناقشه پیشنهاد کرد. روسیه این قطعنامه را علیرغم حمایت 11 عضو از 15 عضو شورا، از جمله کشورهای عضو دائم فرانسه و بریتانیا، وتو کرد. پیش نویس ایالات متحده ماموریت را برای یک سال تمدید می کرد، "رفراندم" را از نام آن حذف می کرد و پیشنهاد خودمختاری مراکش را تنها مبنای مذاکرات بیشتر قرار می داد. اکتبر گذشته، شورای امنیت سازمان ملل قطعنامه ای را تصویب کرد.

news.originalContent:
Massachusetts could take down a 2024 gun law rammed through the state legislature in the aftermath of a landmark Supreme Court ruling if a campaign by pro-Second Amendment activists succeeds Tuesday.

After the Supreme Court struck down New York’s discretionary system for issuing concealed carry permits in New York State Rifle and Pistol Association v. Bruen in June 2022, Massachusetts began the process of altering its gun laws to comply with the high court’s decision. Like other states who had “may issue” systems for issuing permits similar to New York’s, however, Massachusetts’s lawmakers seized the opportunity to enact additional restrictions on law-abiding gun owners. Furthermore, outside backers of the legislation, such as Moms Demand Action, spoke at rallies and events held by anti-Second Amendment groups, according to Gun Owners Action League (GOAL). (RELATED: ‘AK Guy’ Roasts Dem Over Ad Supporting Blue State’s Gun Ban)

The police are three minutes away. What do you do until they arrive? Protect your right to protect your family. Vote No on 9 on November 3. #NoOn9 #Massachusetts #CivilRights https://t.co/Ewf9nVZ3Xe

Pro-Second Amendment activists, such as the Gun Owners’ Action League (GOAL), previously secured nearly 100,000 signatures to put a referendum on the 2026 Massachusetts ballot to ask if Bay State voters supported H.4885, a gun-control law passed in 2024. Such a move would normally block the law from taking effect until after the referendum, but Democratic Gov. Maura Healey had added an emergency provision Oct. 1 to keep the law in force.

Lawmakers added provisions in the legislation that further restrict modern semiautomatics, imposing registration criteria that targeted certain muzzleloaders, added new license requirements to own any semiautomatic firearm, imposed new stipulations on home-built firearms, and added training prerequisites for those seeking carry permits.

Nonresidents were also made to have to jump through additional hoops, including the requirement to acquire a “temporary” license to carry, as well as having to register all firearms and comply with the state’s serialization requirements. The legislation even made it impossible for an out-of-state resident to take any child hunting in the state.

“GOAL has serious concerns about the exemptions in § 129C being used properly by the state. Nonresidents found in possession of firearms have been treated so harshly in MA since the passage of Ch 135 [sic], that GOAL’s worry is that even if one can prove they’re transporting the proper firearms in the proper manner, it will not insulate them from prosecution,” the pro-Second Amendment group states on its website, responding to a February 2026 legal opinion from a partnering attorney. “While these exemptions should prevent such a situation, the current legal climate created by Ch 135 could still result in many hours and funds being spent on defending oneself in court.”

Neither GOAL nor the Massachusetts Coalition to Prevent Gun Violence responded to requests for comment from the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Most Massachusetts voters appear to support the gun-control measure, with 70% of respondents to a poll released by the MASSInc Polling Group saying they were inclined to vote “yes” on the measure, which would allow it to remain in force. The survey of 800 likely voters was conducted from Sept. 14-22 for the CommonWealth Beacon.

news.originalContent:
President Isaac Herzog must tap a candidate to form a new government after results are certified by November 10, with fraught negotiations likely to follow.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his coalition’s parliamentary majority following legislative elections on October 27.

But a bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu also failed to win a majority in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving Israel without a clear path to a new government.

What’s ahead is likely weeks of political wrangling as Israel’s disparate factions weigh possible governing arrangements, including a unity government bringing rival factions together or a minority government reliant on outside support. If they fail to reach an agreement, Israel could head back to the polls.

Here’s what you should know:

The pro-Netanyahu coalition won 53 seats:

A bloc of Jewish parties opposing Netanyahu won 48 seats:

Arab-led parties won 19 seats:

That leaves all existing blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, meaning some parties would have to realign or join forces across bloc lines to form a new government.

Israel’s election results must be officially certified and presented to President Isaac Herzog by November 4.

The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

Herzog must task one incoming Knesset member with forming a new government by November 11. He is expected to make his decision with input from party leaders, selecting the candidate he believes has the best chance of building a coalition.

The candidate commissioned by Herzog has 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible extension of 14 days.

He has not said yet, but the most likely candidates are Netanyahu or former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, whose Yashar party received the most votes in the opposition bloc.

According to Israel’s Yedioth Ahronoth media, Eisenkot may have an edge over Netanyahu as some Arab-led parties consider endorsing him in a bid to oust Netanyahu.

Herzog, for his part, has urged Israeli politicians to move away from rigid partisan stances and look for “creative solutions” that will lead to a new government and avoid a second round of elections.

Before the election, Herzog said he would do everything he could to spare the country another election cycle, even if that means pressing for a national unity government that brings together rivals Netanyahu and Eisenkot.

Eisenkot and other opposition leaders have previously ruled out partnering with the Arab-led parties.

Former Prime Minister Ehud Barak, however, has said he believes they “can change their mind”, arguing that Netanyahu would do in their position.

“If Netanyahu had a similar problem, he would immediately invite Mansour Abbas”, the leader of Ra’am and “give him the role of a minister of interior”, Barak told France 24 on Friday.

Abbas himself has signalled a willingness to work the opposition camp, saying Eisenkot’s conditions would not pose an obstacle for his party, according to Israel’s Channel 12.

Yousef Jabareen from the Arab-led Joint List has also said that his party is ready for the “ousting of the Netanyahu government”.

“The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership,” he wrote on X.

Even if Arab-led parties do not formally join the opposition’s coalition, they could prop it up from outside by helping it pass a confidence vote in the Knesset.

Raluca Ganea, co-founder of Israeli civil society group Zazim, told Al Jazeera that a coalition between the opposition bloc and the Arab-led parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel “is the only path forward for Israeli democracy as a whole”.

If Herzog’s first candidate fails to form a government within the 42 days, the Israeli president has the option of asking another Knesset member to try to do so within 28 days. If that candidate also fails, a majority of Knesset members could put forward a third candidate, who would have a final 14 days to try to assemble one.

Even without a coalition commanding at least 61 seats, a candidate could still try to form a minority government by relying on outside support from smaller parties, including Arab-led parties, or negotiate a power-sharing arrangement with alternating prime ministers.

If none of these options succeed and deadlock persists, the Knesset would be formally dissolved, and Israelis would return to the polls for another round of elections.

Those elections would have to be called within 90 days.

Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed.

If the process drags out, that could leave Israel’s longest-serving prime minister in power for months more, even if he ultimately fails to become part of the next governing coalition.

رئیس جمهور اسحاق هرتزوگ باید پس از تایید نتایج تا 10 نوامبر، با مذاکرات پرتنش در پی آن، نامزدی را برای تشکیل دولت جدید انتخاب کند. بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست وزیر اسرائیل، اکثریت پارلمانی ائتلاف خود را پس از انتخابات قانونگذاری در 27 اکتبر از دست داد. اما بلوکی از احزاب یهودی مخالف نتانیاهو نیز نتوانست اکثریت را در 120 کرسی کنست به دست آورد و اسرائیل راهی روشن برای تشکیل دولت جدید نداشته باشد. آنچه در پیش است احتمالاً هفته‌ها کشمکش سیاسی است زیرا جناح‌های ناهمگون اسرائیل ترتیبات احتمالی حکومتی را بررسی می‌کنند، از جمله یک دولت وحدت که جناح‌های رقیب بیرونی را گرد هم می‌آورد یا یک دولت اقلیت حمایت می‌کند. اگر آنها نتوانند به توافق برسند، اسرائیل می تواند به پای صندوق های رای برگردد. آنچه باید بدانید در اینجا آمده است:
ائتلاف حامی نتانیاهو 53 کرسی به دست آورد:
بلوک احزاب یهودی مخالف نتانیاهو 48 کرسی به دست آورد:
احزاب تحت رهبری عرب 19 کرسی به دست آوردند:
این امر باعث می‌شود که همه بلوک‌های موجود از 61 کرسی مورد نیاز برای اکثریت در کنست برخوردار نباشند، به این معنی که برخی از احزاب برای تشکیل یک دولت جدید باید دوباره متحد شوند یا در خطوط بلوک متحد شوند. نتایج انتخابات اسرائیل باید به طور رسمی تایید شود و تا 4 نوامبر به رئیس جمهور آیزاک هرتزوگ ارائه شود. کنست جدید قرار است در 10 نوامبر سوگند یاد کند. هرتزوگ باید یکی از اعضای کنست را مامور تشکیل دولت جدید تا 11 نوامبر کند. انتظار می رود او با نظر رهبران حزب تصمیم خود را بگیرد و نامزدی را که فکر می کند انتخاب کند.
